prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universally “best” broker for everyone — the right broker depends on where exactly you live (Missouri vs Kansas), what kind of coverage you need (ACA/Marketplace, Medicare, individual/family, small‑group, COBRA, short‑term, etc.), whether you want an independent broker who can show multiple carriers, and whether you prefer in‑person help.

If you tell me your ZIP code and the type of plan you need, I can find and recommend several well‑rated brokers or navigators near you. Meanwhile, here’s how to find a good one and what to ask:

How to find the right broker
- Decide independent vs captive: Independent brokers represent many carriers and can compare options; captive agents work for one insurer.
- Use official resources:
  - For Marketplace (ACA) help: HealthCare.gov or local assister/navigator programs (free).
  - For Medicare: Medicare.gov’s agent/broker finder or your State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP).
  - State insurance department websites (Missouri or Kansas) to verify licensing and file complaints.
- Look at local reviews (Google, Yelp), Better Business Bureau, and LinkedIn for experience and client feedback.
- Ask for references from clients with similar needs.

Questions to ask any broker
- Which carriers and plans do you work with? Are you independent?
- How are you compensated (commission from insurers or fee from me)?
- What experience do you have with people in my situation (age, health needs, doctors/network)?
- Will you compare total monthly costs, deductibles, copays, OOP max, and drug formularies?
- Do you help enroll and handle claims or disputes after I pick a plan?
- Can you provide examples of plans you would recommend and why?

Red flags
- Pushes a single plan without comparing alternatives.
- Vague about compensation or reluctant to put recommendations in writing.
- No state license number or poor reviews about claims handling.

If you share:
- ZIP code
- Whether you’re in Missouri or Kansas
- Type of coverage (ACA individual/family, Medicare, employer plan, small business, etc.)
I’ll compile a short list (3–5) of well‑rated local brokers or free navigator options and include quick notes on which is likely best for your situation.
